issues.description: getCategoryLabel heuristic silently mangles category IDs that don't fit its rules
issues.detail: The old code had an explicit map from ID to label (E3, IAM, Forensics Ready, Trust Boundaries, etc.) and a fallback. The new code throws away the map and replaces it with a 3-rule heuristic: special-cases dict (empty), version-suffix regex, short-word uppercase, otherwise capitalize. Concrete regression: 'trustboundaries' used to render 'Trust Boundaries' (from the map); now it renders 'Trustboundaries'. Similarly any future multi-word category that lacks a hyphen will be silently wrong. Data dominates: the previous data structure (an explicit label table) made the algorithm trivial and correct; the new algorithm is fighting the data shape because hyphenation is unreliable. Restore the explicit table and use heuristics only as fallback.

issues.description: Empty SPECIAL_CASES dict shipped as a placeholder is unearned abstraction
issues.detail: SPECIAL_CASES is exported as an empty Record with only commented-out examples. This is framework-where-library-would-do: the dictionary is the right data structure, but it's been emptied so the heuristic can take over. Either populate it with the real special cases (trustboundaries -> Trust Boundaries, forensics-ready stays fine, etc.) and use it as the primary lookup, or delete the empty scaffolding. As written it adds an indirection layer that does nothing.

issues.description: horizontal-bar-chart width and displayPercentage calculations duplicate logic and recompute Math.max per row
issues.detail: maxValue = Math.max(...data.map(d => d.value)) is now computed inside the .map() iteration, so it's recomputed for every row instead of once. Hoist it above the map. Also the calculatedWidth and displayPercentage expressions share the same fallback chain (item.percentage ?? derived) and could be one helper. n is small so the perf cost is irrelevant; the readability cost is the real issue — two near-identical ternaries next to each other invite drift.

issues.description: SEVERITY_ORDER gains a duplicate 'Info' alias instead of normalizing input
issues.detail: Adding Info: 4 alongside Informational: 4 papers over an upstream inconsistency — somewhere data flows in as 'Info' instead of 'Informational'. The data structure now has two keys meaning the same thing; future severity additions risk drift. Cleaner fix: normalize 'Info' -> 'Informational' at the boundary (adapter), keep one canonical key in the order map.

issues.description: CategorySelector handles 'all' and '' as equivalent — only one is reachable
issues.detail: handleValueChange treats value === '' || value === 'all' as the clear case, but the SelectItem only ever emits 'all' or a categoryId. The empty-string branch is dead. Either document why it's defensive or drop it; small but the kind of cleverness audit Pike's rules call out.

issues.description: data-table-filter-custom passes a formatted label into getBadgeLabel where a raw value was expected
issues.detail: Previously getBadgeLabel(entity, value) received the raw value; now it gets displayLabel (already formatted). If getBadgeLabel does any lookup or transformation on the value (it takes entity + value for a reason), it will now see the human-readable string instead of the ID. Worth confirming getBadgeLabel's contract — this looks like a subtle data-shape change at a seam.

review.summary: The PR is mostly small, composable changes — the categories.ts extraction is the right move and CategorySelector is appropriately small. The core concern is WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE: the previous adapter had an explicit ID-to-label table (the right data structure — algorithm was self-evident), and the refactor replaced it with a three-rule heuristic plus an empty SPECIAL_CASES dict. That's fighting the data shape: 'trustboundaries' regresses from 'Trust Boundaries' to 'Trustboundaries', and any future non-hyphenated multi-word ID will silently misrender. Restore the explicit table as the primary lookup and keep the heuristic as fallback only. Minor cleanups in horizontal-bar-chart (hoist Math.max, dedupe the percentage ternaries) and a normalization-at-boundary fix for the Info/Informational duplication in SEVERITY_ORDER would also tighten things up.
